A personal concept film about food waste, told by the dinner itself.A personal concept film about food waste, told by the dinner itself.

In 42.6 seconds it moves from the plate to the fridge to the bin, and the typography changes with it.

The challenge

Food waste is a numbers story, and numbers are hard to feel:

  • 1 billion meals are thrown away every day, and 60% of food waste happens at home
  • Everyone agrees it is a problem; nobody thinks it is them

The approach

The film gives the numbers a narrator: the dinner itself. It goes from the plate to the fridge to the bin, and the type goes off with it.

"That's enough" is said once as an excuse and given back at the end as a demand: ENOUGH.

The details

  • Seven acts, seven moves: land, print, push, rot, reveal, still, slam
  • A printed receipt, decaying type and rolling counters
  • Timed to a measured voice on a 76 BPM grid
  • Three typefaces: Bricolage Grotesque, Instrument Serif and JetBrains Mono
  • Every move is a real keyframe, with no expressions

Personal concept project. Concept, script and motion by Vivek Kumar. Images are AI-generated (Google Flow) and the voices are AI-generated (ElevenLabs). Music: "Sad" by The Mountain (Pixabay). Data: UNEP Food Waste Index Report 2024 and FAO, The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World 2026.

how it landed

OutcomeOutcome

A personal concept film, so these are the results it is designed for, not live numbers.

What I delivered

  • A 42.6-second vertical film, 1080 × 1920
  • Seven acts, each with its own motion device
  • A visual system of five colours and three typefaces
  • Boards on the premise, structure, art direction and motion

How I’d measure success

  • How many viewers watch to the end
  • Shares and saves of the film
  • Whether viewers remember the line "that's enough"

What it shows

  • Kinetic typography that carries a story
  • Turning data into something people feel
  • Art direction of one subject in six states
  • Motion timed to voice and music
